clue.text: Snipe's Testament or Friar's Lantern ?

definitions.meaning: a group of snipe is a wisp, so the birds' testament is the will of the wisp
an old country name for the flickering marsh light that leads travellers astray

explanation.surface: A list of curious titles, a bird's last will set beside a monk's lamp.
explanation.walkthrough: The first half works because a wisp is the collective noun for a flock of snipe, and a will is a testament.
explanation.definitionFit: Both names describe the ghostly light over marshes; the first is a pun on a will belonging to a flock of snipe.

clue.text: Marriage being its key ceremony

parts.note: the married state is seen as a lock whose ceremony is a wedding: wed plus lock

explanation.surface: A remark that the wedding is the central rite of married life.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue splits the answer as WED, the ceremony, and LOCK, the thing a key opens.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is an old term for the married state, a union of husband and wife.

clue.text: Silly fellow, look out! It will catch you

indicators.note: look out is read as look placed outside the next piece

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or behold
an ass is a foolish person

explanation.surface: A warning shouted to a fool that a trap is about to snare him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'look out' reads as a warning shouted at the fool, but 'out' is the signal for one word to wrap around the other.
explanation.definitionFit: A cowboy's rope with a running noose is thrown to catch animals.

clue.text: Like Endymion, heed no alarm ?

parts.note: Endymion of Greek myth slept forever, so he would sleep through any alarm clock

explanation.surface: A sleeper as deep as the shepherd of legend ignores the alarm.
explanation.walkthrough: In Greek myth the moon goddess Selene put the shepherd Endymion into an everlasting sleep.
explanation.definitionFit: To sleep past the time one meant to wake is what happens when the alarm goes unheeded.

clue.text: Evelyn boxed with Pandora

definitions.meaning: Evelyn is the dead girl in Robert Browning's poem whose surname is the answer
when Pandora opened her box all evils escaped and only one thing stayed inside

explanation.surface: A girl called Evelyn fought a match against Pandora.
explanation.definitionFit: Browning wrote 'Evelyn Hope', and in the myth expectation of good was the gift left in Pandora's box.

clue.text: We raise a flower to discover a beastly transformation

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: in a down clue, raise means the word is read upwards, from bottom to top

explanation.surface: We grow a flower and find it turns into something monstrous.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'raise' means the word is read from the bottom up, so FLOWER turns into REWOLF; 'flower' looks like a bloom, but it is used only for its letters.
explanation.definitionFit: In folklore a man transformed into a wolf under the full moon is a beast-changeling.

clue.text: React to a pistol shot on or off track

definitions.text: React to a pistol shot on or off track

parts.words: React to a pistol shot on or off track
parts.note: anyone jumps when a gun goes off, and on the running track the gun signals runners to begin

explanation.surface: Someone flinches at a gunshot, whether at an athletics meeting or elsewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: On a track the pistol begins the race; off it, a shot makes anyone jump.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a sudden jump of surprise and the beginning of a race.

clue.text: Thrashed as the young shaver should be

definitions.meaning: to lather is old slang for beat or flog

definitions.text: as the young shaver should be
definitions.meaning: a young shaver is a boy, but a man shaving should have soap foam on his face

explanation.surface: A naughty boy got a beating, as boys deserve.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means beaten soundly, and also covered in soapy foam before a shave.

clue.text: Darby and Joan might qualify for Essex side

definitions.text: Darby and Joan might qualify for Essex side

parts.words: Darby and Joan might qualify for Essex side
parts.note: a devoted old couple could win the side of bacon awarded at Dunmow in Essex to couples who never quarrel

explanation.surface: An elderly couple might be picked to play for the Essex county team.
explanation.walkthrough: Darby and Joan are a proverbial happily married old couple; the Dunmow prize in Essex goes to couples who have not quarrelled for a year and a day. 'Side' looks like a sports team.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a salted side of bacon, the prize given at Great Dunmow.

clue.text: But Fido's off-colour with it

parts.note: a dog's viral illness makes Fido off-colour, while the same word is a water-based paint, which suits 'colour'

explanation.surface: A remark that the family dog is poorly with some ailment.
explanation.walkthrough: The name for a canine disease is also a kind of wall paint, so 'off-colour' plays on both the illness and the paint.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a contagious canine disease and also a distemper paint used on walls.

clue.text: Profit from an old tip

parts.note: the article an gives the letter A
vail is an archaic word for a tip or gratuity given to a servant

explanation.surface: Making money out of a piece of advice handed down from long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tip' suggests advice, but here it is a gratuity; VAIL is an obsolete word for such a payment.
explanation.definitionFit: To avail is to be of use or benefit, so it means to profit, as in 'it will avail you nothing'.

clue.text: Player is carried in the boot perhaps

indicators.note: something carried in a container sits inside it, so one piece goes within the other
perhaps tells us the word boot is only one possible arrangement of its letters

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A footballer, or some other player, gets driven somewhere in a car's boot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' turns BOOT into OBOT, and 'carried in' puts the word 'is' inside it. 'Player' sounds like sport, but here it means a musician.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who plays the oboe in an orchestra is a type of musical performer.

clue.text: As one Tabitha did with her tail when vexed ?

definitions.text: As one Tabitha did with her tail when vexed ?

parts.words: As one Tabitha did with her tail when vexed
parts.note: Beatrix Potter's cat Tabitha has a surname describing how a cross cat flicks its tail, read as a verb and the word it

explanation.surface: A cat called Tabitha shows annoyance by moving her tail.
explanation.walkthrough: Mrs Tabitha Twitchit is a cat in Beatrix Potter's children's stories; her surname, split as a verb plus 'it', says what an annoyed cat does with its tail.
explanation.definitionFit: A vexed cat jerks its tail, and the cat's surname spells out that jerking action.

clue.text: Vital part of a young marshal-to be

parts.note: a kid is a young child, so a young one
Michel Ney became one of Napoleon's marshals, so as a boy he was a marshal-to-be

explanation.surface: Something essential to a youngster who is destined to become a marshal.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'a young marshal-to-be' as 'kid Ney': the boy who would grow up to be Marshal Ney of France.
explanation.definitionFit: The kidney is an essential bodily organ, a part the body cannot do without.

clue.text: Old copper turned upside down by the new ?

definitions.text: Old copper turned upside down by the new ?

parts.words: Old copper turned upside down by the new
parts.note: the old penny was written d, from a Roman coin's name; the letter d upside down is p, the new decimal penny

explanation.surface: An old policeman gets knocked over by a new recruit.
explanation.walkthrough: Britain's pre-1971 penny was abbreviated d, for a Roman coin; the decimal penny is p, the same letter turned upside down. 'Copper' suggests a policeman.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman coin's initial was the symbol for the old British penny, the copper coin.

clue.text: There are few fellows like him in Government

definitions.text: There are few fellows like him in Government

parts.words: There are few fellows like him in Government
parts.note: read as rule by a small group: a member of a government made up of only a few men

explanation.surface: A compliment on a rare politician, unlike any other in office.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface praises a man as unique; the cryptic reading is literal, a government run by a few fellows like him.
explanation.definitionFit: Such a ruler belongs to a small clique that holds power, from Greek words for few and rule.

clue.text: An angel has it cooked and served cold

indicators.note: cooked suggests the letters are worked over into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A heavenly being prepares a dish to be eaten chilled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' asks for AN ANGEL plus IT to be rearranged. The definition is loose: the answer is a dish served cold.
explanation.definitionFit: A boned, stuffed meat dish set in aspic is presented chilled, so it is a dish served cold.

clue.text: Dismissed a legislator — it might cause an explosion

parts.note: to be fired is to be dismissed from a job
MP is a Member of Parliament, a British lawmaker

explanation.surface: A politician has been sacked and fears the fallout could be explosive.
explanation.definitionFit: Methane gas in coal mines can ignite and blow up, so it is an explosion risk.

clue.text: Citizens take in £25 in return for giving a general view

indicators.note: in return means everything built so far is read from right to left
the citizens take another piece in, so it goes inside them

parts.note: a cit is an old short word for a citizen or townsman
a pony is British slang for twenty-five pounds

explanation.surface: Townsfolk accept a modest payment in exchange for an overview.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in return' reads CITPONYS backwards. 'Cit' is an old, sneering word for a townsman, and a pony is British slang for twenty-five pounds.
explanation.definitionFit: A synoptic account presents a summary, taking in the whole subject at a glance.

clue.text: Musketeer to seek gold Chinese vessel

parts.note: Sam is the soldier in Stanley Holloway's monologue who refuses to pick up his musket
to pan is to wash river gravel in search of gold

explanation.surface: One of Dumas's swordsmen goes prospecting and boards an Eastern boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Musketeer' suggests Athos and company, but this is Sam Small of the comic monologue 'Pick oop tha musket, Sam'.
explanation.definitionFit: A small flat-bottomed boat used on Chinese rivers and harbours.

clue.text: They may be gay, yet like all flesh just grass

definitions.meaning: dashing young men about town were once called gay ...
the Bible says all flesh is grass, and grass is made of slender leaves

explanation.surface: Young bucks may be merry, yet they are mortal like everyone else.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means lively young men and also the narrow leaves of grass, recalling Isaiah's 'all flesh is grass'.

clue.text: Shallow cousin was no stout fellow

definitions.meaning: in The Merry Wives of Windsor, Justice Shallow has a foolish cousin of this name
someone thin and slight is the opposite of stout

explanation.surface: A timid relative was no brave man.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names Shakespeare's Master Slender, and means thin, the opposite of stout.

clue.text: Wonders about distance in which car reverses

indicators.note: in which places the next piece inside the distance word

parts.note: miles are a measure of distance

indicators.note: the car reverses, so the word car is read backwards

explanation.surface: Amazement at the distance a car covers going backwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reverses' turns CAR into RAC. 'Wonders about' reads like a verb phrase, but 'Wonders' is a noun and 'about' is only a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Marvels or wonders are events beyond natural explanation, such as those of saints.

clue.text: Indian takes money for the basket

parts.note: the Cree are a Native American people of Canada
L stands for pound, from Latin libra, a unit of money

explanation.surface: A Native American is paid to hand over a basket.
explanation.definitionFit: A wicker basket used by anglers to hold caught fish.

clue.text: Foreign articles about a seaman misdescribe him

indicators.note: about means the articles go around the next piece

parts.note: un and le are French words for 'a' and 'the'
le is a French definite article
AB stands for able seaman, a rating in the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: Some foreign grammar about sailors gets the description of a seaman wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer describes an able seaman as the opposite of able, so it misdescribes the AB placed inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling an able seaman incapable gets him exactly wrong, which is how the word misdescribes him.

clue.text: Pinched — a jellyfish can't be

definitions.meaning: British slang for stolen, like pinched
a jellyfish has no skeleton, so it cannot have its bones removed

explanation.surface: A remark that something was stolen, and a jellyfish could never be.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means stolen in slang, and also with bones removed, impossible for a spineless sea creature.

clue.text: Shorter than short cheese

indicators.note: shorter than means the word for short loses a letter at its end

parts.note: brief means short in duration

explanation.surface: A cheese described as smaller than small.
explanation.walkthrough: BRIEF, meaning short, is made shorter by losing its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A soft French cheese with a white rind is a familiar example of a cheese.

clue.text: Syllabuses include some hard words

indicators.note: the word includes some letters, which sit inside it in a run

explanation.surface: School course outlines contain some difficult vocabulary.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits inside 'syllabuses' as letters four to eight.
explanation.definitionFit: Insulting or harsh language is abusive speech, so hard words.

clue.text: The garden air is subtly charged

indicators.note: subtly suggests letters quietly shifted into a different order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: The atmosphere in a garden feels delicately loaded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'subtly' asks for the letters of GARDEN AIR to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To be arraigned is to be formally accused in court, that is, charged.

clue.text: His the age of make-believe

parts.note: split into an age word, old, and a claimant to the throne who makes believe he is king

explanation.surface: Someone belongs to the era of fairy tales and pretending.
explanation.walkthrough: James Francis Edward Stuart, son of James II, claimed the British throne and was known by this title; 'age' gives OLD and 'make-believe' the claimant.
explanation.definitionFit: The name was given to the Stuart claimant to the crown, the elder of two Jacobite pretenders.
